description: A junior Computer Science student with a strong background in high-level languages and theoretical data structures who feels a significant gap in their low-level programming skills.

nodes.title: Systems Programming & Pointer Fundamentals
nodes.description: Introduction to C programming for systems: memory addresses, pointers, and manual memory management basics necessary for OS work.
nodes.personalizationRationale: This student has no prior exposure to systems programming, so we must establish a baseline for C-style memory interaction before OS concepts.

nodes.title: Computer-System Organization Basics
nodes.description: Overview of hardware components (CPU, memory, I/O) and how they communicate via interrupts and buses.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Because the student has no prior exposure, understanding the hardware-software handshake is a prerequisite for studying kernel design.

nodes.title: The Hardware Protection Boundary
nodes.description: Exploration of Kernel Mode vs User Mode and the protection mechanisms used by the CPU.
nodes.personalizationRationale: As a student with no prior exposure, the conceptual jump to dual-mode operation requires dedicated scaffolding to avoid confusion in later blocks.

nodes.title: OS Services and Kernel Structure
nodes.description: Required core content: Operating system services, system calls, and the structural design of kernels (Monolithic vs Microkernel).
nodes.personalizationRationale: This is a core requirement for all students to understand the services and API the OS provides.

nodes.description: The process concept, including Process Control Blocks (PCBs), process state transitions, and context switching.
nodes.title: Process Concepts and Lifecycle
nodes.personalizationRationale: Foundational core material on how the OS manages execution units, mandatory for the exam.

nodes.description: Mechanisms for processes to communicate using shared memory and message passing systems.
nodes.title: Inter-Process Communication (IPC)
nodes.personalizationRationale: Core curriculum requires understanding IPC to prepare for synchronization and networking topics.

nodes.description: Thread models, multi-threading libraries (Pthreads, Windows, Java), and the difference between user and kernel threads.
nodes.title: Threads and Multithreading Models
nodes.personalizationRationale: Core threading concepts are prerequisite to synchronization and scheduling algorithms.
CPU scheduling is a major component of the midterm and final exams.
nodes.title: CPU Scheduling Algorithms
nodes.description: Criteria for scheduling and specific algorithms like FCFS, SJF, and Round Robin.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Mandatory midterm review checkpoint for all students to ensure mastery of foundational blocks.
nodes.title: Midterm Review: Foundations & CPU Management
nodes.description: Comprehensive review and practice problems covering Chapters 1-5 in preparation for the week 8 midterm.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Synchronization is a critical and difficult core topic heavily tested in projects and exams.
nodes.description: The Critical Section problem and the software/hardware solutions including Peterson's solution.
nodes.title: Process Synchronization Basics

nodes.personalizationRationale: Core mastery of synchronization tools is necessary for the concurrent programming assignments.
nodes.title: Synchronization Primitives & Problems
nodes.description: Advanced primitives including Semaphores, Mutexes, and Monitors, and the Dining Philosophers problem.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Core coverage of deadlock management as required by the syllabus.
nodes.description: Deadlock characterization, Prevention, Avoidance (Banker's Algorithm), and Detection.
nodes.title: Deadlock Characterization and Avoidance
Main Memory and Paging
nodes.description: Physical memory organization, fragmentation, and the implementation of paging and page tables.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Core requirement for understanding how the OS manages the physical memory hierarchy.

nodes.title: Virtual Memory Management
nodes.description: Demand paging, page replacement algorithms (FIFO, LRU, Optimal), and thrashing.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Essential core content for the memory management project and final exam.

nodes.description: I/O hardware, application I/O interface, and kernel I/O subsystem performance factors.
nodes.title: I/O Systems and Performance
nodes.personalizationRationale: Core coverage of the I/O subsystem required for the cumulative final.
Required core material on persistent storage management.
nodes.description: File system structures, allocation methods, and free-space management.
nodes.title: File System Implementation

nodes.personalizationRationale: Mandatory final review assessment for this cumulative course.
nodes.description: Final cumulative review of all 7 blocks to prepare for the final exam.
nodes.title: Final Cumulative Review and Assessment
